- [ ] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch

### Module(s)

mini.completion

### Neovim version

0.11.x

### Description

I was trying out the `arduino-language-server` as I wanted to test it in nvim, when I had the lsp working and the completion seemed to be fine I got hit by the next error message while typing:
```
E5108: Error executing lua .../share/nvim/lazy/mini.completion/lua/mini/completion.lua:1820: attempt to index local 'item' (a boolean value)                                                    
stack traceback:                                                                                                                                                                                
        .../share/nvim/lazy/mini.completion/lua/mini/completion.lua:1820: in function 'get_lsp_edit_range'                                                                                      
        .../share/nvim/lazy/mini.completion/lua/mini/completion.lua:1796: in function 'get_completion_start'                                                                                    
        .../share/nvim/lazy/mini.completion/lua/mini/completion.lua:450: in function <.../share/nvim/lazy/mini.completion/lua/mini/completion.lua:425>
```

This occurred while I was typing `std::` after placing the first colon but didn't happen for the second. As the `arduino-language-server` uses `clangd` from behind I was expecting, well, nothing to happen, but this is not exclusive to the `std::` it is something that happens when typing anything that is not a keyword nor a constant.

### Reproduction

 1.  Use `arduino-language-server` with `mini-completion`. Requires clangd and arduino-cli, this is the [arduino_language_server.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21653197/arduino_language_server.txt) I used (I couldn't upload as `.lua`).
> [!NOTE]
> Requires mason

2. Create a `.ino` sketch and try typing anything that could trigger the completion to popup or write random characters, it will also trigger this.

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

I indeed was able to reproduce this (after significant amount of struggle to set up Arduino project). The culprit here is not 'mini.completion', but the LSP server.

In the `std:` situation it returns `{ isIncomplete = false }` output which goes against [LSP specification](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#textDocument_completion) (see `Response` section). The response should be either `CompletionItem[]` (i.e. array/list, which it is not) or `CompletionList` (which [should *always* have `items` field](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#completionList), which it does not).

The reason 'mini.completion' was throwing an error is because it used `pairs()` instead of `ipairs()` to iterate through items (which were inferred as the whole input; since there is no `items` field and hence the input *must* be a list). This resulted into iterating through `isIncomplete, false` key-value pair and resulted in an error.

Usually it is out of 'mini.completion' scope to adjust its code based on LSP server not following the specification. But since using `ipairs()` is more proper here and it fixes the issue, I pushed the fix.

My suggestion would be to also open an issue in Arduino LSP server for them to use the proper data structure in this case.

---

Also, for the future, I'd suggest to be a bit more specific about reproduction steps. They are not bad, don't get me wrong. Just there are steps that assume knowledge with Arduino. Foe example, I struggled with the "Create a .ino sketch" (since I don't have experience with Arduino).

After around five attempts with `clangd` not starting, I've followed [this post](https://ncona.com/2024/02/using-arduino-language-server-with-neovim) ("Setting up Arduino LSP" section) and basically executing 5 CLI commands made it finally work. So it would have been better here to include these steps or link to some documentation that describe those.
